title: Microtoken Horizon: UX ideation and wireframe notes
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a new direction for a token-level cost + latency dashboard that emphasizes temporal patterns and compact at-a-glance diagnostics. The goal of the Microtoken Horizon concept is to let an engineer or product owner spot recent regressions, cluster expensive tokens across invocations, and quickly pivot from surface-level insights to per-invocation forensic detail with minimal clicks.

Design goals (what success looks like):
- Surface short-term regressions and persistent outliers without overwhelming the viewer.
- Provide multi-resolution navigation: daily/last-hour/rolling-100-invocations.
- Compact sparklines + small multiples so many routes/models can be compared in one viewport.
- Fast pivot to a waterfall/tracelet on any selected token or invocation.
- Keyboard-first interactions for power users (navigate rows, open details, export).
- Exportable CSV + JSON of slices for offline analysis.

High-level idea (one-liner):
A timeline-forward dashboard where each route/model row shows a horizon view (sparkline bands + heatmap) of token-level median cost, P95 latency-per-token, and error-weighted tokens; clicking a band drills down to a per-invocation waterfall with replayable tokens and KV cache markers.

Primary screens / wireframe notes:
1) Microtoken Horizon (landing)
- Layout: vertical list of routes (or model+route combos). Columns: route name, uptime SLA badge, micro-horizon panel (60px high), aggregate row metrics (avg tokens, total cost/day, P95 token-latency), quick actions (pin, snapshot, open forensic).
- Micro-horizon panel: horizontally compressed time axis. Each pixel column is an aggregation window (configurable: auto choose between 5m/1h/1d depending on range). Within the column we draw stacked mini-bars: median token-cost (blue), P95 token-latency (amber), error-token density (red overlay). Over the top we can add a thin sparkline of median tokens-per-invocation. Hover reveals a micro-tooltip with exact numbers plus a ‘drill’ link.
- Interaction: keyboard/jump: up/down to move rows, left/right to move time window, Enter to open focused row in Forensic view, "s" to snapshot slice into a saved evaluation.

2) Forensic View (per-route, per-time-slice)
- Header: chosen slice (time range or rolling invocations), top summary: total invocations, total cost, tokens median/mean, top 5 tokens by unit cost impact.
- Main: invocation list (collapseable) with a per-invocation waterfall. Each waterfall row shows token groups (prefix, dynamic, function calls, result) displayed as horizontal token boxes with color encoding for cost intensity and small overlays for latency hotspots. Clicking a token opens a side panel with prompt context, embedding length, KV cache hit info, and model variant used.
- Replay: ability to step through token generation in time (animated highlight) to visualize where latency spikes occur relative to KV fetch/attention kernel switches. 

3) Token Cluster Explorer (aggregate view)
- Show clusters of tokens (by stem, semantic bucket, or token-id) that contribute most to cost. Provide a tag cloud + sortable table with columns: token, estimated unit-cost, frequency, avg-latency, common prefixes.
- Quick action: propose a quantization/slot change or caching hint; ability to add a token rule to Redwood Optimize recommendations.

Micro-interaction & microcopy notes:
- When hovering a micro-horizon band: show small actionable items — Open forensic, Snapshot slice, Add to watchlist. Keep hover delay short (~200ms) to support scanning.
- Use color-blind safe palette; use pattern overlays for error-density rather than relying on red alone.
- For pinned snapshots, allow short descriptions and attach Jira links.

Backlog grooming (candidate tickets and acceptance criteria):
- PROTO-1: Render micro-horizon visual (desktop responsive) with three stacked metrics. AC: canvas renders bands for 50 rows with caching; hover tooltip shows exact numbers; keyboard focus works.
- PROTO-2: Forensic invocation waterfall prototype. AC: clicking a band opens forensic view with at least 20 invocations and token boxes; replay works at 60ms/frame.
- PROTO-3: Token cluster extraction job (backend). AC: nightly job that computes top-100 tokens by daily cost per route, exposed via API.
- PROTO-4: CSV/JSON export for selected slice. AC: export respects time range + filters, downloadable within 3s for <=10k rows.
- PROTO-5: Accessibility checks and color palette adjustments. AC: pass WCAG AA for contrast and test with color-blind simulator.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Aggregation window heuristics: do we default to time-based windows (5m/1h) or invocation-count windows (rolling 100 invocations)? Reasoning: invocation windows are stable for variance per workload, time windows are more intuitive for SREs. Suggestion: allow both and show in UI which is active.
- Cost vs latency normalization: should micro-horizon show absolute cost/latency or z-score normalized per-route? Absolute helps chargeback; normalized highlights regressions across routes with different scales. Proposed solution: show absolute by default, provide normalization toggle.
- Privacy & sampling: storing token-level traces can be sensitive (user data). Must ensure sampling + redaction rules; store token ids only when allowed. Work with Security/Compliance to define retention and redaction policy (linked ticket: jira:PROD-1942).

Edge cases to handle:
- Very high-cardinality routes (1000s of daily invocations): collapse to aggregated rollup with top-N expandable rows.
- Sparse routes (few invocations): show sparse timeline and indicate low confidence in P95 estimates.
- Mixed-model fallbacks: when a request fell back to a cheaper model, mark bands with a small badge and allow filtering to only same-model variants.

Data/schema notes for engineers (brief):
- Endpoint: GET /telemetry/routes/{route}/token-horizon?range=1d&resolution=5m returns arrays: timestamps[], median_token_cost[], p95_token_latency[], error_rate[] plus sample_invocations[]. Aim to keep response < 200KB for 50 rows.
- For forensic view: GET /telemetry/invocations?ids=... returns invocation-level token streams with token-id, position, cost_usd, latency_ms, cache_hit boolean. Consider compressing token streams with RLE for storage efficiency.

Design mock variants to test in research:
- Variant A: Dense horizon with stacked bars (more info density). Good for power users.
- Variant B: Minimal sparklines + heatmap overlay (less cognitive load). Better for execs/product managers.
- Variant C: Table-first with inline micro-horizons (prioritizes readability and keyboard navigation).

Next steps (short-term roadmap):
- Week 0-1: Proto-1 spike — render micro-horizon canvas and wire up keyboard navigation (Benji + Samir).
- Week 2: Backend aggregation API spike + token clustering prototype (Marta).
- Week 3: Forensic view prototype + replay (Aisha + Eve).
- Week 4: Usability sessions with 5 internal engineers; iterate colors and hover latency.
- After spike: produce an MD spec for product PRD and break out engineering tickets.

Notes to reviewers:
- Focus feedback on: 1) Are the three metrics we chose (median-cost, p95-latency-per-token, error-density) the right ones? 2) Is the micro-horizon concept interpretable at glance? 3) Accessibility concerns and sampling/retention policy assumptions.

Slack refs / background threads:
